title: Luke Burton
text:
PhD Researcher · Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology and Dynamics, London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine







Understanding and predicting the behavioural drivers of epidemic dynamics. Also economic evaluation of blood-borne virus screening.

My PhD asks how social contact, mobility and attitude data can be used to understand and help anticipate the behavioural drivers of epidemic dynamics. It builds on a background in mathematics and health data science, and on earlier work using branching process models to estimate the probability that an introduction becomes a major epidemic.
I also work in health economics, on screening for blood-borne viruses.
Current positions:


Visiting Researcher, Imperial College London — Part of the PhD.
Research Assistant, Health Economics (part-time), University College London — NIHR-funded work on cost-utility modelling and economic evaluation of blood-borne virus screening interventions.

title: Research
text:
PhD project

Behavioural drivers of epidemic dynamics
Social contact, mobility and attitude data carry signal about how people actually behave during an outbreak — who mixes with whom, how that changes under pressure, and how quickly it reverts. The question is whether that signal can be used not just to explain epidemic dynamics after the fact, but to help anticipate them.

title: Research
text:
Alongside it

Economic evaluation of blood-borne virus screening
An NIHR-funded project on the cost-effectiveness of blood-borne virus testing interventions: hepatitis B progression modelling for emergency department opt-out testing; TB IGRA testing in high-risk groups; and micro-costing of digitally enhanced testing.
